EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Tensions between the US and Iran remain critically high following President Trump's visit to China, where he discussed Iran's nuclear program and the Strait of Hormuz, indicating potential for further "clean-up" operations in Iran. Concurrently, the Israeli-Lebanese border saw intense exchanges, with Hezbollah launching multiple drone and rocket attacks, causing civilian casualties and an IDF soldier fatality, met by extensive Israeli airstrikes on Hezbollah infrastructure. Regional diplomatic efforts, including a failed BRICS joint statement due to disagreements over the Iran conflict, highlight deep divisions.

IRAN
President Trump, after his visit to China on 15 May 2026, reiterated his stance on Iran's nuclear program, stating that a 20-year suspension would be acceptable but demands "real commitment" and the removal of all "nuclear dust" from the country. He suggested a need for a "small clean-up operation" in Iran following a ceasefire and claimed 80-85% of Iran's missile launchers and production capability have been destroyed, dismissing intelligence reports to the contrary as "fake news." Trump indicated he would "soon" decide on lifting sanctions on Chinese companies purchasing Iranian oil, signaling a potential deal. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, during a press conference in New Delhi, emphasized that Iran has no trust in the US, will only enter "genuine negotiations" if the other side is serious, and is ready for any scenario. He stated that the Strait of Hormuz remains open for friendly nations, requiring only coordination with Iranian forces, and that Iran will fulfill its historical role as a security guardian. Araghchi also confirmed that Iran received Washington's response to its 14-point proposal, which was rejected, leading to a "deadlock" on the enriched material issue. The BRICS foreign ministers' meeting ended without a joint statement, with Araghchi blaming a member country's support for the US-Israeli aggression against Iran, specifically the hosting of US bases, for the lack of consensus. Iranian military officials, including Army Chief Major General Amir Hatami, asserted the armed forces' readiness to defend Iran's territorial integrity and respond to aggression. The Iranian Parliament's National Security Commission proposed a 50 million Euro reward for killing Donald Trump, Benjamin Netanyahu, and the CENTCOM commander. Reports of an oil spill in the Persian Gulf near Lavvan Island were circulated. Iran’s Space Agency announced three domestically developed satellites are in final testing.

ISRAEL
Israeli forces and the home front faced significant hostile activity, particularly from Lebanon. On 15 May 2026, Hezbollah launched approximately 10 drones at northern Israel, leading to sirens in the Galilee Panhandle and Western Galilee, with two drones intercepted and others falling in open areas, causing no injuries in Kiryat Shmona and Metula. However, one drone attack near Rosh Hanikra earlier resulted in one civilian critically wounded and another moderately wounded. A fire broke out in agricultural areas near Rosh Hanikra due to intercept debris. On 14 May 2026, a barrage of rockets from Lebanon targeted Kiryat Shmona, with some intercepted and others landing in open areas without injuries. An IDF soldier, Staff Sgt. Negev Dagan, 20, of the Golani Brigade's 12th Battalion, was killed by Hezbollah mortar fire in southern Lebanon last night (14 May 2026). The IDF also intercepted a rocket fired from Lebanon at the Lower Galilee on 15 May 2026, triggering sirens in Masad and Eilabun, and successfully intercepted a rocket fired at IDF forces in southern Lebanon. Politically, Prime Minister Netanyahu stated Israel controls 60% of the Gaza Strip, hinting at further expansion. The IDF conducted a snap drill, "Sulfur and Fire," on the Jordanian border on 15 May 2026, simulating terrorist infiltrations and drone attacks, with 100% reservist turnout in the 96th Division's volunteer brigades. Clashes erupted in Jerusalem's Old City on Jerusalem Day, with 7 arrests. Domestic incidents included a fatal road accident on Road 1 killing an infant and seriously injuring three adults, and a fatal hit-and-run in Kiryat Ata. Housing prices in Feb-Mar rose by 0.3%, with new home prices up 0.4% (or down 0.3% excluding buyer-subsidized apartments).

GAZA & WEST BANK
Prime Minister Netanyahu stated that Israel currently controls 60% of the Gaza Strip. In the West Bank, an IDF Unit 636 killed a masked assailant throwing stones at Israeli vehicles near Luban al-Sharqiya in the Shomron Brigade area, pursuing another. Settler activities included the burning of a mosque and vehicles in Kafr Jibia, north of Ramallah, on the night of 14 May 2026. Palestinian Authority President Abu Mazen was re-elected Fatah chairman at 90 years old and appointed his son, Yasser, to a key Fatah leadership role, seen as an attempt to establish him as a successor. The humanitarian situation in Gaza was described as critical, with reports of increased Israeli abuse and sexual torture of Palestinian prisoners, a claim Israel's PM Netanyahu and FM Sa'ar are reportedly suing the New York Times over.

LEBANON
Hezbollah escalated its operations, launching multiple drones, rockets, and mortars against northern Israel and IDF positions in southern Lebanon on 15 May 2026. Incidents included about 10 drones targeting the Galilee Panhandle and Western Galilee, with impacts in Kiryat Shmona and Metula, and an explosive drone strike near Rosh Hanikra injuring two civilians (one critical, one moderate). Another rocket launched at the Lower Galilee was intercepted. Earlier, on 14 May 2026, Hezbollah fired a barrage of rockets at Kiryat Shmona. An IDF soldier, Staff Sgt. Negev Dagan, was killed by Hezbollah mortar fire in southern Lebanon on 14 May 2026. Hezbollah also attempted to shoot down an Israeli Air Force drone over southern Lebanon with a surface-to-air missile, which "failed." In response, the IDF conducted extensive airstrikes, targeting Hezbollah infrastructure in the Tyre area, Zebdine (destroying a rocket launcher used for Kiryat Shmona attacks), Al-Qusayyah, Kharayeb, and Burj Qalawiyah. Over the past 24 hours, the IDF reported striking 65 Hezbollah infrastructure sites and eliminating over 20 operatives. Over the past week, the IDF claimed to have struck over 440 targets and killed more than 220 Hezbollah operatives in southern Lebanon. Evacuation warnings were issued for several Lebanese villages on the outskirts of Tyre ahead of these strikes. Reports also noted the use of phosphorus bombs by Israeli forces on Al-Taher.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Iraq's Parliament officially approved a new government under Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi on 15 May 2026. US CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper claimed the new Iraqi Prime Minister pledged to distance Iraq from Iran. Several Iraqi political blocs, including Al-Fayyad's alliance, Al-Asadi's alliance, and Al-Aqad Al-Watani, announced their withdrawal from Al-Sudani's coalition, indicating political instability. Iraqi Joint Operations Command reported a successful drone strike (CH5) in Wadi Al-Shay, Kirkuk, against a "dangerous terrorist element," destroying a hideout and killing the target. Iraqi "Islamic Resistance heroes" claimed to have targeted sensitive sites deep within the "Zionist entity" with drones, achieving accurate and direct hits. Air traffic was launched against Iranian "terrorist opposition parties" in Dohuk and Erbil provinces in northern Iraq, specifically targeting the Kurdistan Freedom Party. The UN Deputy Secretary-General called for investment in Syria's reconstruction, noting improved humanitarian access and returning refugees, but warned of reduced funding.

GULF STATES
The UAE unsuccessfully attempted to persuade neighboring countries, including Saudi Arabia and Qatar, to coordinate a joint military response against Iran following US-Israeli attacks on Iran beginning 28 February 2026. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Qatari Emir Tamim bin Hamad reportedly refused, stating it was "not their war," causing frustration in the UAE. The UAE maintained that it reserves all sovereign, legal, diplomatic, and military rights to respond to any threat from Iran and is accelerating the construction of a new oil pipeline bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, expected to be operational by 2027, to double its export capacity from Fujairah. Saudi Arabia is reportedly considering signing a non-aggression pact with Iran and other regional countries, similar to the "Helsinki Accords." US Energy Secretary Chris Wright predicted the Strait of Hormuz's importance for global oil and gas transport would decline due to new pipeline capacities. A South Korean destroyer departed for the Gulf of Aden on 15 May 2026, for rotational missions supporting maritime security.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US-Iran Tensions Escalation:** President Trump stated he would decide "soon" on lifting sanctions on Chinese companies buying Iranian oil but maintained Iran must cease all nuclear activities and commit to a "real" 20-year suspension, rejecting Iran's latest proposal.
2.  **Increased Hostilities on Israel-Lebanon Border:** Hezbollah launched multiple drone and rocket attacks, including approximately 10 drones on northern Israel, resulting in one civilian critically wounded and another moderately wounded near Rosh Hanikra, and the death of IDF Staff Sgt. Negev Dagan, 20, by mortar fire on 14 May 2026.
3.  **Extensive Israeli Retaliatory Strikes:** The IDF reported striking over 65 Hezbollah infrastructure sites and eliminating over 20 operatives in southern Lebanon in the past 24 hours, and over 440 targets and 220 operatives over the past week, including a rocket launcher in Zebdine.
4.  **BRICS Meeting Deadlock:** The BRICS foreign ministers' meeting in New Delhi concluded without a joint statement on 15 May 2026, due to differing views on the Middle East, specifically a member country's support for US-Israeli aggression against Iran, as stated by Iran's FM Araghchi.
5.  **UAE Strategic Shift:** The UAE sought a coordinated military response against Iran from Saudi Arabia and Qatar (who refused), and is accelerating a new oil pipeline project to bypass the Strait of Hormuz by 2027.
6.  **Iraqi Government Instability:** Iraq's new government under PM Ali Falih Al-Zaidi was approved, but faced immediate withdrawals from key political blocs (Al-Fayyad, Al-Asadi, Al-Aqad Al-Watani).
7.  **US Military Preparedness:** The IDF conducted a snap drill "Sulfur and Fire" on the Jordanian border on 15 May 2026, simulating sudden events and demonstrating 100% reservist turnout, following lessons from 7 October 2023.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of escalation in the Iran war is critically high, particularly with President Trump's statements hinting at further military "clean-up" operations in Iran and his demand for genuine and permanent cessation of nuclear activities. The failure of the BRICS meeting to issue a joint statement underscores deep regional and international divisions regarding the conflict, suggesting a lack of a unified diplomatic front. The Israel-Lebanon border remains an active flashpoint, with Hezbollah's persistent drone and rocket attacks, including civilian casualties and an IDF fatality, guaranteeing ongoing Israeli retaliation. The IDF's extensive strikes and high alert status indicate preparation for sustained or intensified conflict. The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical choke point, with high oil prices reflecting the market's concern over its closure, despite Iran's claims of safe passage for friendly nations. US and Chinese calls for its opening, combined with the UAE's efforts to bypass it, highlight its strategic importance and vulnerability. Political instability in Iraq, marked by withdrawals from the new government's coalition, could create further power vacuums or opportunities for proxy activities, increasing spillover risks.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States:** President Trump, returning from China, expressed conditional openness to a 20-year suspension of Iran's nuclear program but demanded a "real commitment" and removal of "nuclear dust." He reiterated that a military solution against Iran had been effective and might require further "clean-up," despite earlier claims of not wanting to continue the war. He stated he would decide "soon" on lifting sanctions on Chinese oil companies buying Iranian oil. CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper denied reports of Iran retaining 70-75% of its missiles, deeming them "inaccurate," and stated that the new Iraqi PM pledged to distance from Iran.
**China:** Foreign Minister Wang Yi announced President Xi Jinping accepted Trump's invitation to visit the US in autumn. China agreed with the US that the war must end and the Strait of Hormuz must be open, but appeared unwilling to deeply intervene without concessions from Washington. China is seen as having significant influence over Iran due to oil purchases.
**Germany:** Chancellor Friedrich Merz spoke with President Trump, agreeing Iran must come to the negotiating table, open the Strait of Hormuz, and be prevented from acquiring nuclear weapons.
**Egypt:** The Foreign Minister, in talks with Russia's FM, emphasized commitment to a diplomatic path between the US and Iran and continued efforts to de-escalate regional tensions.
**Pakistan:** The Foreign Minister announced the repatriation of 11 Pakistani and 20 Iranian citizens who were on US-seized vessels. Trump acknowledged halting the war with Iran "as a favor to Pakistan."
**United Kingdom:** Iran's embassy in London condemned new UK sanctions as "unfounded" and "politically motivated."
**Spain:** Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced Spain's boycott of the 2026 Eurovision Song Contest in protest of Israel's participation.
**Japan:** The Prime Minister, in a call with the US President, stressed the need to de-escalate Middle East tensions.
**South Korea:** Deployed a 4500-ton destroyer from Busan to the Gulf of Aden for rotational missions to escort South Korean vessels and support international maritime security efforts.
**BRICS Nations:** The foreign ministers' meeting in New Delhi ended without a joint statement, attributed by Iran to a member country's stance on the US-Israeli conflict with Iran.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
There are significant contradictions in reporting and statements regarding the extent of damage to Iran's military capabilities. President Trump claims 80-85% of missile launchers and production are destroyed, dismissing "intelligence reports" to the contrary as "fake news," while CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper stated that reports of Iran retaining 70-75% of its pre-war missiles are "inaccurate." This suggests either conflicting assessments within the US administration or deliberate narrative shaping.

Propaganda indicators are present in both US and Iranian messaging. Trump's "clean-up" rhetoric and claims of easy military victory, along with Iran's Parliament offering bounties for US/Israeli leaders, are examples of assertive posturing. Iran's FM Araghchi's strong denial of US trustworthiness and repeated claims of Iran as a reliable partner in Hormuz can be seen as an effort to counter US narratives.

Reporting gaps exist regarding the specific "14-point proposal" from Iran and the exact reasons for the US's rejection, beyond a general non-acceptance of nuclear activities. The details of the "complex incidents" simulated in the IDF's "Sulfur and Fire" drill at the Dead Sea are vague. The precise nature and extent of the alleged oil spill near Lavvan Island in the Persian Gulf also lack detailed confirmation beyond one source's "if authenticity is confirmed" caveat. The full implications of the withdrawals from Iraq's new government coalition are also yet to be fully clear.
